title: Keep recent items out of a retest
statement: When students sit an adaptive test again, exclude the items they answered recently and cap each item's exposure, letting both rules give way before either could stop a session.
example: One assessment meant for repeated interim use had a mean between-session overlap of 29.4%, with 38 items above 30% exposure.
detail: An adversarial review of a reading assessment meant for repeated interim use found a mean between-session overlap of 29.4%, 38 items above 30% exposure and 289 of 786 items never used in the latest simulation, and the package's own limits section says students who take it more than once will see repeated items (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`). The fix excludes items a student answered in their last 2 sessions, with a three-stage fallback (relax to the last one, then off, plus an unfiltered retry mid-session) so that exposure control can never stop a session starting or end one early, and it demotes over-cap items to a second selection tier rather than excluding them (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/ADDRESS_STATUS.md`). The design-review procedure makes both a hard constraint for repeat sittings (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/skill/SKILL.md`).
against: Neither mechanism is switched on yet: both ship off by default, enabling them needs a simulation re-run, and a recheck called the overlap disclosed and not blocking a one-session pilot but still a real exposure at a later stage (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RECHECK_FINDINGS.md`).

evidence.quote: Repeated interim measurement is the entire point, yet mean between-session overlap is **29.4%**, 38 items exceed 30% exposure, and 289/786 items were never used in v4.
Item security is weaker: students who take the test multiple times will see repeated items (mean pairwise between-session overlap 29.4%)

**retest-overlap exclusion** — items a candidate answered in their last 2 sessions are excluded from selection, with a three-stage starvation fallback (relax to last-1, then off, plus a mid-session unfiltered retry) so exposure control can never prevent a session from starting or end one early
**per-band exposure soft caps** — over-cap items are demoted to a second selection tier, never hard-excluded.
Both new mechanisms ship **off by default** — pre-committed for the calibration ("regular use") stage, not the pilot.
repeat sittings require retest-overlap exclusion + per-band exposure caps
Disclosed; not blocking a 1-session pilot; still a real Stage-3 exposure.
